bull.t: Broad-based revenue growth and raised guidance
bull.b: Strong growth across multiple products, including oncology, Xywav, Epidiolex and Zepzelca, reduces reliance on a single near-term driver. The raised full-year outlook and record quarterly revenue indicate durable commercial execution and expanding demand over the next several quarters.

bull.t: Resilient cash generation and improved leverage
bull.b: Consistently positive operating and free cash flow gives Jazz resources to fund clinical development, acquisitions and commercial investment internally. Meaningfully lower leverage and substantial cash also improve financial flexibility, supporting resilience if product competition or development spending increases.

bull.t: Ziihera approval expands the oncology platform
bull.b: The first-line Ziihera approval broadens Jazz’s addressable oncology opportunity and establishes a new treatment option supported by Phase 3 survival improvements. Combined with existing Ziihera uptake and other oncology growth, it strengthens portfolio diversification and future commercial potential.

bear.t: Oxybate franchise faces generic and emerging competition
bear.b: Jazz’s sleep portfolio is a major revenue contributor, so future generic penetration or adoption of competing orexin therapies could pressure volume, pricing and patient retention. Even with limited generic uptake so far, management expects market dynamics to require ongoing monitoring.

bear.t: Margin pressure and rising operating investment
bear.b: Higher royalties on Zepzelca and Modeyso are weighing on gross margin while increased SG&A and R&D raise the cost base. Continued investment may support growth, but unless revenue scales faster than these expenses, operating leverage and earnings conversion could remain constrained.

bear.t: Planned commercial leadership transition creates execution risk
bear.b: The planned change affects a senior role responsible for commercial execution across specialized neuroscience and oncology markets. A successor search creates potential continuity risk over the next several quarters, particularly as Jazz launches products and manages increasingly complex portfolio priorities.
